verses.text: David left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's family heard about it, they went down to him there.
All those who were in trouble or in debt or unhappy gathered around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
From there David went to Mizpah in Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and mother come and stay with you until I learn what God will do for me."
So he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him as long as David was in the stronghold.
But the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go into the land of Judah." So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
Saul heard that David and his men had been found. Saul was sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in his hand, and all his officials were standing around him.
Saul said to them, "Listen, men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

Is that why you have all plotted against me? No one tells me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you cares about me or tells me that my son has stirred up my servant to wait in hiding to attack me, as he is doing today."
But Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's officials, said, "I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelek son of Ahitub at Nob.
Ahimelek asked the LORD what David should do. He also gave him food and the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
Then the king sent for the priest Ahimelek son of Ahitub and all his family, who were the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.
Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." "Yes, my lord," he answered.

Saul said to him, "Why have you plotted against me, you and the son of Jesse? You gave him bread and a sword and asked God for help for him, so that he has turned against me and lies in wait for me, as he does today."
Ahimelek answered the king, "Who among all your servants is as faithful as David? He is the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, and highly respected in your house.
Was that the first time I asked God for help for him? Of course not! Please do not blame your servant or any of my family, because your servant knows nothing at all about this whole affair."
But the king said, "You will surely die, Ahimelek, you and your father's whole family."

Then the king ordered the guards beside him, "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was running away, yet they did not tell me." But the king's officials would not raise a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
The king then ordered Doeg, "You turn and strike down the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck them down. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
He also attacked Nob, the town of the priests, with the sword. He killed its men and women, its children and babies, and its cattle, donkeys and sheep.
But Abiathar, a son of Ahimelek son of Ahitub, escaped and ran away to join David.
He told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
Then David said to Abiathar, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am to blame for the death of your father's whole family.
Stay with me and do not be afraid. The man who wants to kill you also wants to kill me. You will be safe with me."
